known_matplotlib_xerr_issue.detail: export_20260911/GATE2_REPORT.md documents an unresolved 'ValueError: xerr must not contain negative values' failure in mediation/pretrend plotting when a bootstrap CI does not contain its own point estimate. The current psm_260915.py (git commit a7c52db, 2026-09-15, after the Gate 2 run) already replaces every Axes.errorbar(xerr=/yerr=) call with a custom _plot_point_estimates_with_intervals() helper (lines 5582 on) that draws the CI as an explicit line segment instead of a +/- offset, and so cannot raise this error. scripts/make_report.py still scans stderr/logs for the xerr/yerr failure signature defensively (never assume a fix holds without observing it), but does not expect to find it.

per_year_2012_2018.match_rate_trend_note: Match rate falls from 99.9% (2012) to 51.9% (2018) because reuse_controls_across_years=false: a control matched in an earlier year is unavailable to later years, so the eligible pool for each successive index year thins out relative to demand. Generator quotas must reproduce declining treated counts (21,754 -> 14,594) but roughly stable eligible-control counts (13.2-13.4M every year) for this dynamic to emerge naturally from the pipeline's own matching, not be hand-coded into the generator.

matching_edge_preflight.max_candidate_real_edges_note: The task prompt text quotes 98,612,946 for this cell; the source CSV's own candidate_real_edges value for this exact (t0=2012, age 65-69, no prior rehab, sex 1) row is 98,612,694. Per Hard Rule 7 ('the file wins if we disagree'), 98,612,694 is used everywhere in this bundle.
matching_edge_preflight.admissible_share_definition: candidate_real_edges / (n_treated_in_stratum * n_controls_in_stratum). Scale-free (does not change with sampling fraction), which is what makes it usable to compare a synthetic run at ANY fraction against the real 20% matching load -- unlike candidate_real_edges itself, which scales with the square of stratum size and is therefore useless for cross-scale comparison.
matching_edge_preflight.admissible_share_pattern: Near-total admissibility (92.7-99.2% in the top-20-by-edges table below) in age 60-74, no-prior-rehab strata, where both treated and control propensity scores are bunched near 0 (divorce is rare at these ages, so almost nothing separates treated from control on the propensity scale, and nearly every pair falls inside the 0.01 caliper). Sparse admissibility (3.2-6.4%) in age 45-54, no-prior-rehab strata, where scores spread out over roughly 0-0.3+ and the caliper excludes most pairs. This pattern is what a calibrated generator's latent divorce-propensity function must reproduce; a generator whose covariates barely predict divorce will bunch ALL strata near total admissibility (the Gate 2 synthetic-data failure mode described in GATE2_REPORT.md and in the task brief), inflating edges quadratically with sample size instead of the ~5x-per-100x-rows growth the real data shows between its worst 1%-scale stratum (20,707,718 edges, Gate 2) and its worst 20%-scale stratum (98,612,694 edges, this file).

gate2_reference_memory_points.caveat: GATE2_REPORT.md explicitly attributes the >100x edge growth from Gate 1 to Gate 2 (200,234 -> 20,707,718 for 10x rows) to the OLD generator's score-bunching artifact, not to the estimator or real data (the real 20% data's worst-stratum growth from the 1% synthetic worst stratum is under 5x: 20,707,718 -> 98,612,694). Once this bundle's generator passes the Step 3 admissible-share calibration check, its own 0.1%/1% memory peaks (measured locally and then on Workbench) supersede these Gate 2 numbers as the basis for projecting 10%/100% -- these are a fallback only for scripts/memory_gate.py when no local run yet exists.
